answer: One concrete defense is reputation that must be earned through verified work over time, like a marble sinking slowly through a nebula: a new identity cannot vote or move markets until it has a checkable trail of useful transactions. A sybil swarm then hits an echo problem — thousands of fresh accounts all sound identical, with no history behind them, so the network weights only identities whose past work can be verified, making fakes expensive to build and easy to spot.
